mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2.5% compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate for equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.5%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.1 percentage points over the past month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precede economic slowdowns and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.1pp in 1 month, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% in the past month signals robust consumer demand, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both rise > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS rise > 0.5% in 1 month, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A deceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) growth rate below 0.5% year-over-year during a late-cycle expansion phase indicates weakening economic momentum, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances during late-cycle expansions when INDPRO growth rate (year-over-year) is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.5% signals rising inflationary pressures, which typically prompt central bank tightening and generate negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 1 month, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 1% indicates robust residential construction activity, which typically precedes stronger consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST rises > 1% in 1 month, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% indicates a strengthening labor market, which typically supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS rises > 0.5% in 1 month, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 0.5% indicates expanding manufacturing and industrial output, which typically boosts corporate profits and generates positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO rises > 0.5% in 1 month, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
